userJob: Import the token stylesheet where every component can see it
problem: Tokens are declared in a CSS module, so the class name is hashed and the properties are scoped to the element that class lands on, and components above it cannot read them
worksWhen: Any React project built with Vite
avoidWhen: The project routes tokens through a Tailwind theme layer, where adding a stylesheet is a second system
mechanism: Import one token stylesheet from the entry module that calls the root render, above every component import. In development each imported stylesheet is injected as its own tag in import order; the build concatenates them, so an order that looks right while you work can invert once built. Check the built output, not only the dev server.
risks: A cascade order that only holds in development
Two token systems, one in the stylesheet and one in the Tailwind theme, so half the components move when one changes
mobileRules: An inverted cascade in the build usually shows first where responsive overrides live, which is at 375px
accessibilityRules: Colour tokens for both schemes belong in the same file so the dark scheme is measured rather than inferred

userJob: Find out how this project already writes CSS before adding any
problem: A styling approach is chosen by preference, so a project with CSS modules gains a plain stylesheet or a Tailwind project gains a module, and the two systems then compete for the same elements
worksWhen: Any existing React project you did not scaffold
avoidWhen: A genuinely empty project, where you are choosing the first strategy and should say so
mechanism: Read the strategy off the project. A Tailwind config file or a Tailwind import line means Tailwind, and tokens belong in its theme layer. Any module stylesheet means CSS modules, and every new file follows that naming. Neither means plain stylesheets. Never add a second strategy alongside the first.
risks: Adding the second strategy for one component, which becomes the precedent for every later one
Deciding from the package manifest alone, when the manifest can list a dependency the project no longer uses
mobileRules: Mixed strategies produce responsive overrides in two places, which is where the conflict first becomes visible
accessibilityRules: Competing strategies commonly clobber focus indicators, so verify the indicator after any strategy change
genericnessNote: Reading the existing convention is the opposite of imposing a style.

userJob: Handle a plan that needs a second page in a plain React and Vite project
problem: A second route is assumed to exist, so a router gets installed uninvited and the project gains a dependency and a routing model nobody asked for
worksWhen: Any Vite React project with no framework routing
avoidWhen: A router is already installed, where using it is correct
mechanism: The root index.html is the real entry, not a template and never something to move into the public directory. It loads one module that mounts into one element. If the plan needs a second route, check the package manifest for a router already installed. If there is none, say so in the report rather than installing one.
risks: Installing a router to satisfy a plan the brief did not ask for
Moving the entry HTML into the public directory, which breaks the build in a way that reads as a config error
accessibilityRules: If a router is added later, route changes need focus moved to the main region, which a single-page app does not do by itself
genericnessNote: A structural fact about the stack.

userJob: Point the render matrix at the running development server
problem: The default port is assumed, the dev server took the next one because the default was busy, and the matrix captures whatever else is on the default port
worksWhen: Every verification pass in this stack
avoidWhen: Never; reading the port costs one line of output
mechanism: Read the port off the startup output every time rather than assuming it. Anything only the build changes needs a production build and the preview server before the matrix counts.
risks: A pass captured from an unrelated application that happened to be serving the default port
Reporting a development-only result for something the build changes
accessibilityRules: An accessibility pass against the wrong origin is worse than no pass, because it produces a green result

userJob: Recognise the React and Vite failures that only appear after the build or after deploy
problem: Development is correct and the build is not, so the failure arrives at the worst point in the run and looks like a design regression
worksWhen: Diagnosing anything that works in development and fails later
avoidWhen: Never; all three are silent in development
mechanism: Tailwind content globs skip extensions they do not list, so classes vanish in the build while development stays correct. Strict mode mounts twice in development only, so an effect that measures the DOM reports doubled values the preview will not show. An asset referenced as a bare string path rather than an import is never copied into the output and fails only after deploy.
risks: Fixing a doubled measurement by dividing it, which breaks the production build
Concluding a class does not exist when the glob simply did not scan its file
mobileRules: A missing class from an unscanned file is often a responsive variant, so the failure appears at one width only
accessibilityRules: A missing built class can remove a focus style that was present in development, which no build step reports

userJob: Load a typeface in a Vite project without a late shift or a stale cache
problem: The face is imported from inside a component stylesheet, so it is discovered only after the module graph loads, and that is the layout shift
worksWhen: Any Vite React project with a custom face
avoidWhen: The face is served by the host under the client's own licence and loading strategy
mechanism: Self-host the font files, import them through the bundler so they are hashed, and preload the above-the-fold face from the head of the entry HTML. Files placed in the public directory ship unhashed, so a cached copy goes stale silently.
risks: An unhashed font file that browsers keep serving after it is replaced
Preloading every weight, which competes with the first paint it was meant to protect
mobileRules: The shift rewraps every line at 375px, which is where a late face is most visible
accessibilityRules: Verify the weights the scale assumes exist in the face, since a synthesised weight loses contrast
genericnessNote: A loading mechanism does not choose the face.
